subject: Billing entity fallback and net-terms clause — Acme order form redlines
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines — invoicing / net terms

Jordan — attaching redlines to the order form from Procurement. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) We need Net60 payment terms (Acme standard) rather than Net30/Net45.
2) Invoicing must be addressed to Acme Inc (US entity) for services used here; however finance may withhold taxes depending on our country of record. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a consolidated HQ invoice if we provide intercompany allocation details, and whether you can supply a W-8/W-9 equivalent or tax residency docs.

Also flagged: minimum commit proration. We prefer monthly proration for ramp months rather than counting full committed month.

Files attached: Acme_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf; Acme_Tax_Certificate.pdf

Thanks — please advise next steps and timeline.

Regards,
Jane Doe
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
procurement@acme.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Team — forwarding Acme's redlines (attached). TL;DR: they want Net60, invoicing to US entity, possible withholding/tax certificate, and monthly proration for minimum commits on ramp.

Questions / ask list: 
- Legal (Kim): can we accept Net60? If not, what language can we offer (Net45 standard + finance review for Net60 with PO)? Also need to advise on the invoicing entity fallback language (they insist invoices go to Acme Inc but may route payments through Acme Global Holding).
- Finance (Laura): operationally, can we issue consolidated HQ invoices or do we need separate invoices per paying entity? What docs do we require to avoid withholding?
- Sales (Ben): are we OK to accept monthly proration for ramp months or do we want to push quarterly minimums? Also any commercial sensitivity on committing to Net60?

I've attached the redlines and the procurement email. Goal: respond to Acme with a single proposal by Monday EOD Pacific.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form redlines — invoicing / net terms

Jordan / team — reviewed Acme's redlines. High level legal input below: 

1) Net terms: we generally standardize on Net45 for new enterprise deals. Net60 requests are acceptable only with finance sign-off and a PO referencing the order form. Recommend we propose: "Net45; Net60 available upon receipt of an approved PO and confirmation of remittance instructions from the paying entity." This preserves negotiating leverage and aligns with our AR risk policy.

2) Invoicing entity & fallback clause: Acme asks that invoices be addressed to Acme Inc (US). We should include fallback language to ensure Redwood may invoice the contracted Redwood entity and Acme must provide timely remittance instructions. Suggested clause: "Customer shall provide written remittance instructions and identify the paying entity. If invoices are not paid by the identified paying entity within X days after due date, Redwood may reissue invoices to the contracting entity or the Customer's parent and pursue collection without waiving rights under this Agreement." I'm happy to draft a tracked-changes version.

3) Tax withholding: Acme's request for tax residency docs is normal. We should request their tax certificate (they provided one) and confirm whether withholding is expected. If withholding applies, we will not gross-up pricing; instead the customer is responsible for any withholding unless a different arrangement is documented.

4) Minimum commit proration: legal is neutral on proration; commercial decision. If we accept monthly proration, add language to state how usage will be measured and pro-rated on a daily basis for the first invoice period.

Action: I'll attach a short markup with the proposed language (OrderForm_Markup.docx). Jordan — if Finance confirms Net60 ops, I'll incorporate Net60 PO path into the clause.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form redlines — invoicing / net terms

Team — finance ops perspective: 

1) Invoicing / entity mapping: We can issue invoices to Acme Inc (US) and also support consolidated HQ invoicing, but need an entity mapping table and confirmation of intercompany allocations (SOW-Attachment.xlsx helps). If they want a single HQ invoice that allocates usage to subsidiaries, Acme must provide recurring allocation templates and remittance instructions. 

2) Net60: Operationally doable but requires: (a) an approved customer PO referencing the Redwood order form; (b) a credit check / underwriting (we can fast-track on existing customers); (c) a signed ACH/wire authorization or confirmed bank details. Until those are in place, we should treat Net45 as default.

3) Tax & withholding: If Acme will withhold, we require their tax certificate and completed W-8/W-9 equivalent to release us from gross-up obligations. If withholding applies, we will deduct the withholding amount from the payment due to Redwood (no gross-up). Provide them a remittance address and account details for US invoicing.

4) Late payments & fallback: propose a 15-day cure window and then Redwood may suspend services or reassign invoices to another entity per Legal's suggested clause. Also recommend we include a clause requiring payment method updates before Net60 is approved.

Attachments: SOW-Attachment.xlsx

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations & Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — invoicing / net terms

Hi Jane — thanks for the redlines and the tax cert. Quick summary and proposal from Redwood below. Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow if helpful.

Proposal (one-pager):
- Net terms: Standard Net45. Net60 available upon submission of a customer PO referencing the Redwood Order Form, completed remittance instructions, and confirmation of bank details; Finance to approve within 3 business days once docs received.
- Invoicing entity: Redwood will invoice Acme Inc (US) as requested. If Acme requests consolidated HQ invoicing, Acme must provide the allocation template and entity mapping in writing; Redwood will issue a consolidated invoice only if allocations and remittance instructions are provided at signature.
- Withholding taxes: Acme's tax certificate received — thank you. If withholding is required by Acme, Redwood's pricing will remain unchanged and Acme is responsible for any withholding amounts (no gross-up). We request formal confirmation of withholding obligations prior to invoicing.
- Minimum commit proration: Redwood accepts monthly proration for ramp months. Usage will be measured daily and prorated on the first invoice period as: (actual usage / days in month) * committed monthly amount.
- Late payment fallback: 15-day cure period; if unpaid, Redwood reserves the right to reissue invoices to the contracting Redwood entity or Customer parent and suspend services per the agreement.

Next steps / action items:
1) Jane: confirm whether you will provide a PO for Net60, and confirm whether withholding will apply.
2) Acme Finance: if you prefer consolidated HQ invoicing, please send the allocation template and confirm the paying entity.
3) Kimberly / Laura / Ben: please review the proposed one-pager and let me know if you want any edits. I'll send to Acme once we have a short sign-off here.

Thanks all — aim to finalize and return to Acme by Wed EOD.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
